day_shape: 79 items: Iran-US MoU signed 18 June under strain with Iranian military reportedly ordering Strait of Hormuz closure and Tehran accusing Washington of breaching clause one, Vance and Araghchi in Switzerland, IDF names fourth soldier killed in Hezbollah tank strike and reports 50+ rocket ceasefire violations, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU and Switzerland talks
threads.summary: Iranian and US delegations arrived in Switzerland with VP Vance leading the US side and Araghchi meeting Swiss FM Cassis in Burgenstock, with Qatari and Pakistani mediators slated to shape the format. Iranian negotiator Bagheri said the US has not implemented the first clause of the 18 June memorandum, while Trump was reported as calling the deal Iran's unconditional surrender.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz closure claim
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Iran's top joint military command ordered the Strait of Hormuz closed in response to alleged US breach of the MoU, while Vance disputed the closure claim. Intertanko said 80 mines must be cleared before normal shipping can resume.

threads.label: Iranian hardliner pushback on talks
threads.summary: IRGC Supreme Leader representative Hajisadeghi said negotiation is not the main option and General Rezaei warned optimism would be exploited by the enemy. Iran International reported a hardline MP read excerpts of purportedly top-secret Khamenei letters opposing US talks on state TV before the broadcast was cut.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon tank strike and ceasefire
threads.summary: The IDF named Staff Sgt. Nave Habshoosh as the fourth soldier killed in a Hezbollah drone/anti-tank attack on a 401st Brigade tank, alongside Sgt. First Class Nir Ben Ari killed in a separate overnight strike that injured 13. The IDF said Hezbollah launched 50+ projectiles in ceasefire violations, struck dozens of sites overnight, and continued operations around a Tebnit tunnel system while Netanyahu said troops would stay as long as necessary.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes on Hamas operatives
threads.summary: The IDF announced it killed Ahmed Samir Muhammad Washah, an Al Jazeera photojournalist it identified as a Hamas sniper, in a strike in central Gaza's Bureij area alongside two other operatives. A separate strike in southern Gaza killed Hussein Qadra and Mohammed Farra, whom the IDF said diverted over half a billion shekels to Hamas's military wing via couriers in Turkey and Gaza.

threads.label: Iran domestic rights and shortages
threads.summary: Iran International reported lawyer Javad Alikordi was sentenced to 18 years in prison over a memorial for his brother, and detailed shortages hollowing out Iran's legal drug market into illicit channels. A separate report cited state welfare data indicating nearly one-third of registered adoptions over the past decade were illegal.

events.summary_en: Change of time for PhD entrance examination interviews. To provide the opportunity for PhD examination applicants to participate in the farewell ceremony and funeral procession of the martyred leader of the Islamic Revolution at universities and higher education institutions accepting students, the interview time, which was 13 to 17 Tir, has been moved to the days of the following week from 20 to 24 Tir.
